comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Evidence from [rebar:2876-7958-8dee-4882] that likely explains some overlap-judge failures.

The 8 `overlap-judge` failures recorded in `/tmp/03ef-review6.out` were NOT judge-logic failures.
They were `status_code: 401 authentication_error` on `model=anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6` — a
DIRECT-ANTHROPIC call issued by a project configured entirely for Bedrock.

Root cause (proven on 2876): `overlap/judge.py` binds its model with
`resolve_model_string(STANDARD_CLASS)` threading no `repo_root`, and the LLM config table was
discovered from the ambient cwd/`REBAR_ROOT` rather than from the gate's pinned code root. When
ambient discovery missed the project's `rebar.toml`, `parse_class_slots({})` returned the
built-in bare-Anthropic defaults, so the judge called direct Anthropic and 401'd. `judge_one` /
`judge_batch` swallow ANY exception as an abstain (deliberately — the overlap step is advisory
and must never fail a review), so the failure surfaced only as "the judge abstained", not as a
provider misroute.

Consequence for this ticket: overlap-judge failure counts collected BEFORE the fix are
contaminated. An unknown share of them are this misroute rather than a judge problem, and
because the failure path is a silent abstain they are indistinguishable in aggregate. Re-measure
after change https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1494 lands before drawing conclusions
about judge quality.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
CORRECTION to my previous comment, so it is not read as more than it is: this ticket's signature is a SLOW failure (312-381s, requests=3), whereas the 2876 misroute fails in 0.2s at authentication. They are different failure modes and the 401s are NOT the timeouts described here.

What survives: the misroute means an unknown share of overlap-judge calls in pre-fix runs went to a different provider than the one they were recorded against, and every judge failure — fast or slow — is swallowed as a silent abstain (`judge_one`/`judge_batch` catch Exception). So pre-fix ABSTAIN counts are contaminated and the provider attribution on them is unreliable. The 312-381s timeouts remain unexplained by 2876 and still need their own root cause.

## Not the same bug as [rebar:895c-3eb2-043a-4de1] — do not fold them together

While proving 895c's root cause (Bedrock rejecting an over-complex structured-output grammar), a
**second, distinct** LLM failure mode surfaced in the same logs and must not be attributed to it.

### The two are separable on three independent axes

| | 895c (schema complexity) | THIS bug (overlap-judge) |
|---|---|---|
| step | `plan-review-prerequisite-verifier` | `overlap-judge` |
| duration | 180.6-185.9s (tight, 27 samples) | **312-381s** (different band) |
| `requests` recorded | **0** — no model request ever completed (pre-response 400) | **3** — real requests completed |

A pre-response 400 and a failure after three completed requests are different mechanisms. The
duration bands do not overlap.

### What is known

* Recorded via the usage instrumentation landed by [rebar:aec1-76e7-bb95-4c86]: 5 occurrences,
  312-381s, `requests=3`. Overall failure rate across that sample was 64 ok / 9 failed = 12.3%.
* Separately observed in `/tmp/03ef-review6.out`: `llm call [overlap-judge] ... model=anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6 FAILED in 0.4s: status_code: 401 ... 'API key is invalid.'` — a DIFFERENT overlap-judge failure again (direct-Anthropic auth), tracked separately.
* 895c's original report also noted `UnexpectedModelBehavior: Exceeded maximum output retries (2)`
  from the overlap judge — consistent with an output/validation failure rather than a request
  rejection.

### Why it matters

`overlap-judge` deduplicates findings across reviewers. When it fails the review still proceeds,
so this degrades silently — the failure is not visible in the verdict.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] the mechanism behind the 312-381s / `requests=3` overlap-judge failures is established BY
      MEASUREMENT (capture the actual exception and provider body — the existing evidence records
      duration and request count but not the error body)
- [ ] it is confirmed whether this is retry exhaustion, an output-validation failure, or a
      provider-side timeout — the three imply different fixes
- [ ] the effect of an overlap-judge failure on the resulting verdict is stated explicitly: what
      silently changes when dedup does not run
- [ ] a regression test drives the identified failure path

## Testing

    python -m rebar.llm.usage_log summarize .rebar/usage.jsonl   # the recorded evidence
    pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q
